title: My home and my city
goal: Describe where you live, compare two things, and say that something exists.
bekal: compare two things with the pattern *af'al ... min*
describe a home and a city in a few connected sentences

dialogs.title: حِوَار — أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟
dialogs.intro: Laila asks Budi where he lives while he is in Cairo.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: Where do you live in Cairo?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: أَسْكُنُ فِي شَقَّةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ قُرْبَ الْجَامِعَةِ.
lines.id: I live in a small apartment near the university.
lines.literal: I-live in apartment small near the-university.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: How many rooms does it have?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: غُرْفَتَانِ وَمَطْبَخٌ وَحَمَّامٌ. هُنَاكَ شُرْفَةٌ أَيْضًا.
lines.baca: ghurfataani wa maṭbakhun wa hammaam. hunaaka shurfatun aiḍan.
lines.id: Two rooms, a kitchen and a bathroom. There's a balcony too.
lines.literal: two-rooms and kitchen and bathroom. there balcony also.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: جَمِيلٌ! هَلْ هِيَ أَغْلَى مِنْ شَقَّتِي؟
lines.baca: jamiil! hal hiya aghlaa min shaqqatii?
lines.id: Nice! Is it more expensive than my apartment?
lines.literal: beautiful! is it more-expensive than apartment-my?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: لَا أَعْرِفُ. أَدْفَعُ ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافِ جُنَيْهٍ فِي الشَّهْرِ.
lines.baca: laa a'rif. adfa'u thalaathata aalaafi junaihin fish-shahr.
lines.id: I don't know. I pay three thousand pounds a month.
lines.literal: not I-know. I-pay three thousands pound in the-month.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: That's much cheaper than my apartment!

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: لٰكِنَّ حَيَّكِ أَهْدَأُ. حَيِّي مُزْدَحِمٌ جِدًّا.
lines.baca: laakinna hayyaki ahda'. hayyii muzdahimun jiddan.
lines.id: But your area is quieter. Mine is really crowded.
lines.literal: but area-your quieter. area-my crowded very.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: كَثِيرًا. هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ مَدِينَتِي، وَأَقْدَمُ أَيْضًا.
lines.baca: kathiiran. hiya akbaru min madiinatii, wa aqdamu aiḍan.
lines.id: Very much. It's bigger than my city, and older too.
lines.literal: much. it bigger than city-my, and older also.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.baca: wa maa ajmalu shai'in fiihaa bira'yik?
lines.id: What do you think is the most beautiful thing here?
lines.literal: and what most-beautiful thing in-it with-opinion-your?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: The people. They're the most generous people I've ever met.

notes: **هُنَاكَ has two jobs.** In unit 3 it meant "there"; here it means **"there is"**: هُنَاكَ شُرْفَةٌ ("there is a balcony"). Position tells them apart — at the start of a sentence it states that something exists. A more formal form: يُوجَدُ ("there is to be found").

**كَمْ takes a SINGULAR noun with tanwin fathah.** كَمْ غُرْفَةً؟ ("how many rooms?"), not كَمْ غُرَفًا. It is the same rule as numbers 11 and up in unit 6 — and just as much against an English speaker's instinct to say "rooms".

**The أَفْعَل pattern for comparing.** كَبِير → أَكْبَر (bigger), غَالٍ → أَغْلَى, رَخِيص → أَرْخَص, هَادِئ → أَهْدَأ, قَدِيم → أَقْدَم, جَمِيل → أَجْمَل. One form for masculine and feminine — no change at all.

**"More ... than" uses مِنْ.** أَكْبَرُ مِنْ مَدِينَتِي. Here مِنْ doesn't mean "from" in the sense of origin; it simply marks what you compare with, like English "than". To strengthen it: بِكَثِيرٍ ("much more").

**"Most" uses the same form, but without مِنْ.** It is built as an iḍafah: أَجْمَلُ شَيْءٍ ("the most beautiful thing"), أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَةٍ ("the biggest city"), أَكْرَمُ نَاسٍ ("the most generous people"). So one pattern covers both "-er" and "-est".

**ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافِ جُنَيْهٍ — numbers stacked.** أَلْف (a thousand) has the plural آلَاف, and it follows the rule for 3–10: the number takes the opposite gender and the noun is plural with kasrah. Large sums of money call for exactly this.
**بِرَأْيِكَ — "in your opinion".** Literally "with your opinion". Other equally common forms: فِي رَأْيِي ("in my opinion"), مَا رَأْيُكَ؟ ("what do you think?").

grammars.title: Comparing: -er and -est

head: Adjective
Comparative
Example
Meaning
rows: my house is bigger than yours

after: Three adjectives that break the pattern and must be memorized: جَيِّد → أَحْسَن (better), سَيِّئ → أَسْوَأ (worse), and كَبِير meaning age → أَكْبَر سِنًّا (older).
Word order decides the meaning: **أَكْبَرُ مِنْ...** = "bigger than"; **أَكْبَرُ مَدِينَةٍ** = "the biggest city"; **اَلْمَدِينَةُ الْكُبْرَى** = "the great city" (a special form, rare at A1).

grammars.title: Saying there is and there isn't
after: Note that whatever "there is" is always **indefinite** (with tanwin): هُنَاكَ مَطْعَمٌ. If you use اَلْ, the sentence turns into one about location: اَلْمَطْعَمُ هُنَاكَ ("the restaurant is over there").

sections.title: The home and what's in it

blocks.text: The word حَمَّام needs attention: in the Arab world it means bathroom **and** toilet at once. If you ask أَيْنَ الْحَمَّامُ؟ in a restaurant, you'll be pointed to the toilet — which is what you meant anyway. A more polite form in public places: دَوْرَةُ الْمِيَاهِ.

blocks.title: Describing a place in three layers
items: The easiest way to describe a place without running out of words: give its **location**, then its **size**, then **what's in it**. أَسْكُنُ فِي شَقَّةٍ قُرْبَ الْجَامِعَةِ. هِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ لٰكِنَّهَا مُرِيحَةٌ. فِيهَا غُرْفَتَانِ وَشُرْفَةٌ.
Those three sentences already let someone picture your place, and they use only material you've had since unit 5.

blocks.text: One word you'll hear a lot: بَلَد. It means "country" **and** "town" at once, depending on context — and وَسَطُ الْبَلَدِ ("the middle of town") is the standard name for downtown almost everywhere in the Arab world.

items: I live in a small apartment.
How many rooms does it have?
My city is smaller than Cairo.
This is the most beautiful city.

exercises.prompt: Compare the two things in one complete sentence.
Describe where you live in six sentences: location, size, contents, the neighborhood, and what you like about it.
items: What's the neighborhood like: quiet or busy?

answers: أَكْبَر — أَصْغَر — أَجْمَل — أَقْدَم — أَسْهَل — أَحْسَن
أَسْكُنُ فِي شَقَّةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ. — كَمْ غُرْفَةً فِيهَا؟ — هُنَاكَ شُرْفَةٌ أَيْضًا. — مَدِينَتِي أَصْغَرُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَةِ. — هٰذِهِ أَجْمَلُ مَدِينَةٍ. — لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ مُشْكِلَةٌ.

اَلْقَاهِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ جَاكَرْتَا. — اَلشَّايُ أَلَذُّ مِنَ الْقَهْوَةِ. — اَلنَّحْوُ أَصْعَبُ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ. — بَيْتِي أَوْسَعُ مِنْ بَيْتِ صَدِيقِي. — اَلْحَافِلَةُ أَرْخَصُ مِنَ السَّيَّارَةِ.

Example: أَسْكُنُ فِي جَاكَرْتَا — أَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْتٍ صَغِيرٍ — فِيهِ ثَلَاثُ غُرَفٍ وَمَطْبَخٌ — هُنَاكَ حَدِيقَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ أَمَامَ الْبَيْتِ — حَيِّي هَادِئٌ وَنَظِيفٌ — أُحِبُّ الْحَدِيقَةَ لِأَنَّهَا مُرِيحَةٌ
